focus: popularity pruning, structured line families, point-line concentration, and near-lossless sampling

messages.body_markdown: `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` now exposes the weaker mass-only accepted-subgraph interface. This already suffices for reached-root extension and global peeling, while avoiding a whole-line-core hypothesis in the central obligation. If `AE-18` needs $G_0[T]$, that can remain an optional strengthening.
messages.subject: Mass-only core handoff

messages.body_markdown: Round 2 retains the exact requirement $D\le K_\theta d$. Allowing an additional negative power of $\epsilon$ would make $D/d$ unbounded and invalidate the constant-size factor partition used by `IE-L-FACTOR-CONCENTRATE`.
messages.subject: Bounded-weight interface retained

messages.body_markdown: Please audit `IE-L-FACTOR-LIFT` as a standalone seed-point lemma: at one simple point, more than $\Delta$ compatible directions should kill the formal-root terms of degrees $d+1,\ldots,\Delta$; substitution and irreducibility should then give $C\sim Z-Q$. No rejected source is attached as proof evidence.
messages.subject: Exact factor-lift audit

messages.body_markdown: The proposed Vinh-free aggregation works once the seed-point lift is exact: the irreducible factor $C_i$ is fixed globally, so $C_i\sim Z-Q$ charges every point in every disconnected $C_i$-class to the same $Q$. The factor class must explicitly retain $C_i(x,f(x))=0$, as recorded in `IE-L-FACTOR-CONCENTRATE`.
messages.subject: Vinh-free factor aggregation

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence graph
nodes.notes: Every chosen affine parametrization is bijective. All measures use uniform point-line incidence normalization in the fixed prime-field, bivariate scope.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and the affine-line set $\mathcal L_p$. For each $L\in\mathcal L_p$, fix a bijective affine parametrization $L:\mathbb F_p\to L$ and a polynomial $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$. Define $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(L(t),L):L\in\mathcal L_p,\ t\in\mathbb F_p,\ P_L(t)=f(L(t))\},\qquad \epsilon=\frac{|E_{\rm acc}|}{p^2(p+1)},$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d}\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)].$$ For $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$ put $$e(G)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)},\quad \mu(G)=\frac{|X|}{p^2},\quad \tau(G)=\frac{|T|}{p(p+1)},\quad k(G)=\operatorname{mindeg}(G).$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching structured family
nodes.notes: This measures the rank of labeled graph constraints rather than only the number of sampled lines.
nodes.statement_markdown: For an integer $D$ with $d\le D<p$, let $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\},\qquad N_d(D)=\dim V_D,$$ and $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ For $G=(X,T,E)$ define $$N_G(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E\},$$ $$\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)=\{x\in N_G(L):\exists M\in R\setminus\{L\},\ x\in N_G(M)\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<N_d(D)$, and $|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>D$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Popularity pruning
nodes.notes: The source audit verdict is `revise`; the harness determines proof status. The node records the constant-mass two-sided core used by the baseline route.
nodes.statement_markdown: If an accepted carrier $G$ has $e(G)=\delta>0$ and $\tau(G)\le\sigma$, then, for $k_0=\lfloor\delta p/100\rfloor$, it contains $G_0$ with $$e(G_0)\ge\delta/4,\qquad k(G_0)\ge k_0,\qquad \delta/4\le\tau(G_0)\le\sigma.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component concentration
nodes.notes: This is the exact component-measure input for the cardinality-based sampler.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G$ be a connected accepted graph with minimum degree $k$, line measure $\tau$, and $C_*=2^{40}$. If $$k^2\ge C_*dp,\qquad k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\mu(G)\ge\frac{k}{4p},\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.$$

nodes.label: Component-sensitive reaching sample
nodes.notes: The sample loses only absolute constants, but its cardinality remains controlled by the component's line support.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `IE-L-COMP-MEASURE`, writing $t=|T|$, there exists $R\subseteq T$ such that $$\frac{4t}{k}\le |R|\le\frac{16t}{k}$$ and $$|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>\frac12\deg_G(L)$$ for every $L\in T$. Hence $|R|=\Theta(\tau p^2/k)$.

nodes.label: Component-sensitive decoder
nodes.notes: This packages the accepted interpolation, extension, cleanup, and component recovery chain.
nodes.statement_markdown: If a connected accepted graph of minimum degree $k$ and line measure $\tau$ satisfies $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional square-root milestone
nodes.notes: The existence of the required small-line-measure component remains an antecedent, not a proved localization theorem.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $\Lambda\ge1$, and let $G_0$ be a popularity core with minimum degree $\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$. If some connected component of $G_0$ has line measure at most $\Lambda\epsilon$ and $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}\left(\frac dp\right)^{1/2},$$ then one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{\epsilon}{160000}.$$

nodes.label: Support-localization ceiling
nodes.notes: Thus smaller component support alone cannot move the accepted cardinality/root-budget architecture beyond the square-root scale.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $$0<k\le C\epsilon p,\qquad \tau\ge k/(4p),\qquad k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\epsilon^2\ge\frac{C_*}{4C^2}\frac dp.$$

nodes.label: Universal integral-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: This rules out a specific graph-only sparsification principle, not soundness: the same table already has an immediate decoder.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$ there is a legal table with $$\frac1{2K}\le\epsilon\le\frac2K$$ such that every $R$ reaching half of every accepted line satisfies $$|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ while some constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Regular fractional-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: The source audit verdict is `revise`; this is a diagnostic node outside the goal ancestry.
nodes.statement_markdown: There is a legal full-line-support table with $\epsilon=d/p$, every line of accepted degree $d$, every point of accepted degree $d$ or $d+1$, and global decoder $Q=0$. Put $N(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E_{\rm acc}\}$. For weights $\lambda_M\ge0$, require for every line $L$ that $$\sum_{x\in N(L)}\min\left\{1,\sum_{\substack{M\ne L\\x\in N(M)}}\lambda_M\right\}\ge\frac d2.$$ The minimum total weight $W=\sum_M\lambda_M$ satisfies $$\frac{p(p+1)}{2(d+1)}\le W\le\frac{p(p+1)}{2(d-1)}=\Theta\left(\frac p\epsilon\right).$$

nodes.label: Exact two-line concentration identity
nodes.notes: This identifies accepted-degree variance as the correction to the random two-line baseline. The source audit verdict is `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $a_x=|\{L:(x,L)\in E_{\rm acc}\}|$ and $$\Gamma_2=\frac{1}{p^3(p+1)}\sum_x a_x(a_x-1).$$ Then $$\Gamma_2=\epsilon^2-\frac{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}p+\frac{\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)}.$$ In particular, $\Gamma_2\ge\epsilon^2/2$ when $\epsilon\ge2/p$. The variance-free formula is attained by accepting $k$ direction classes, where $\epsilon=k/(p+1)$ and $Q=0$.

nodes.label: Exact-linear endpoint
nodes.notes: The modal construction refutes this uniform endpoint but remains below every fixed $(d/p)^{1-\eta}$ trigger. The source audit verdict is `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown: The assertion that there exist absolute $C,c>0$ such that every legal instance satisfies $$\epsilon\ge C\frac dp\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c\epsilon$$ is false, already for $d=101$.

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal incidence obligation. A proof may start with `IE-L-POPULAR-CORE`, but the sufficient conclusion is intentionally mass-only. Both cover obstructions explain why the decoder alternative is essential.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$ there exist $C_\theta\ge1$, $0<a_\theta\le1$, and $K_\theta\ge1$ such that, if $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\theta},$$ then either $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,$$ or there exist an accepted subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$, a set $R\subseteq T$, and an integer $D$ such that $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d,$$ and $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Near-lossless parameter gate
nodes.notes: The constant $C_\theta$ may be enlarged without weakening the dichotomy. No characteristic-size assumption beyond $d<p$ is introduced.
nodes.statement_markdown: After enlarging $C_\theta$ so that $C_\theta\ge16K_\theta/a_\theta$, the structured branch satisfies $$\frac{D}{\epsilon p}\le\frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\le\frac{a_\theta}{16},\qquad D\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon p}{16}<p.$$ Indeed, for $\rho=d/p<1$, one has $\rho=\rho^{1-\theta}\rho^\theta\le\epsilon/C_\theta$.

nodes.label: Low-rank squarefree interpolation
nodes.notes: Choose a nonzero kernel element and replace it by its squarefree radical. More than $D$ sampled affine lines exclude a $Z$-independent radical; $D<p$ then makes its $Z$-derivative nonzero.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the structured branch there exists a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,
\qquad A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0$$ for every $M\in R$.

nodes.label: Reached-root extension
nodes.notes: The cited step supplies the accepted root-counting template; the rank-producing hypothesis is new upstream.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every line vertex $L$ of $G$, the more than $D$ distinct reached accepted points force $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Primitive content reduction
nodes.notes: This separates content removal from the prime-field vertical-separability input.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content, $B$ is primitive in $Z$, $h=\deg H$, and $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}(B)$. Then $B$ is squarefree and $Z$-dependent, $$d\le\delta,\qquad h+\delta\le D.$$ At most $h$ affine lines satisfy $H(L(t))\equiv0$; every other line vertex of $G$ satisfies $$B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Prime-field vertical separability
nodes.notes: Here $\delta\le D<p<dp$, which is inside the exact separability range of the cited lemma.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `IE-L-PRIMITIVE-REDUCE`, $$\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$

nodes.label: Weighted ramification-line bound
nodes.notes: This is the weighted-resultant estimate applied to the coprime pair $B,B_Z$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $r=\deg_ZB$. The number of degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines satisfying both $$B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0,\qquad B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$$ is at most $$(2r-1)\delta-dr^2\le\delta^2/d-\delta.$$

nodes.label: Prime-field vertical cleanup count
nodes.notes: This sharpens the earlier generic exceptional-edge count and avoids directional-derivative transfer. The formula is written without fraction commands to prevent control-character ambiguity.
nodes.statement_markdown: At most $$h+\delta^2/d-\delta\le D^2/d-D$$ lines are content-trivial or identically $B_Z$-ramified. On every other line, $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, while the nonzero polynomial $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ has at most $\delta-d\le D-d$ roots. Thus deleting all nonsimple accepted incidences costs at most $$(D^2/d-D)/(p(p+1))+(D-d)/p\le D^2/p^2+D/p.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless global cleanup
nodes.notes: Each peeling deletion is charged once to the vertex removed at that stage. The cleanup and peeling costs together are at most $4D/p\le a_\theta\epsilon/4$.
nodes.statement_markdown: After the vertical deletion, iteratively delete every point or line vertex of current degree at most $D$. Peeling costs less than $$\frac{D(|\mathbb F_p^2|+|\mathcal L_p|)}{p^2(p+1)}<\frac{2D}{p}.$$ There remains a nonempty graph $G_1$ satisfying $$e(G_1)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2}\epsilon,\qquad k(G_1)>D,$$ with $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ on every line vertex and $$B(x,f(x))=0,\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$$ at every point vertex.

nodes.label: Simple-root factor partition
nodes.notes: The cited step supplies factorwise $Z$-dependence; its audit verdict is `revise`. The degree-preserving star partition is a separate drafting argument.
nodes.statement_markdown: Factor $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i$$ into distinct irreducibles and put $\Delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_i)$. Primitivity makes every $C_i$ depend on $Z$, so $$s\le\deg_ZB\le D/d\le K_\theta.$$ At a simple lifted point exactly one factor vanishes; every incident line has that same factor identity. Hence the simple-root graph is a disjoint union of factor classes $F_i$, each preserving every vertex degree. For some $i$, $$e(F_i)\ge\frac{e(G_1)}s\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon,\qquad k(F_i)>D\ge\Delta_i,$$ and its vertices satisfy $$C_i(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$$ on every line and $$C_i(x,f(x))=0,\qquad C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0$$ at every point.

nodes.label: Seed-point factor linearization
nodes.notes: At a simple point, use the formal implicit root. More than $\Delta$ compatible directions kill its homogeneous terms from degree $d+1$ through $\Delta$; the resulting degree-$d$ truncation annihilates $C$, and irreducibility should force association. A fresh exact audit is required.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible with $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}(C)\le D<p$. If a nonempty accepted factor class $F$ has $k(F)>D$, satisfies $C(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ on every line vertex, and has $C_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$ at every point vertex, then there exists $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$C\sim Z-Q.$$

nodes.label: Global factor aggregation
nodes.notes: Association to one fixed irreducible factor aggregates all disconnected factor components without point-line mixing or Vinh incidence estimates.
nodes.statement_markdown: For the factor class $F$ from `IE-L-FACTOR-CONCENTRATE`, the identities $C(x,f(x))=0$ and $C\sim Z-Q$ imply $Q(x)=f(x)$ at every point vertex of $F$. Since every affine point lies on at most $p+1$ lines, $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{|X(F)|}{p^2}\ge e(F)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Close the direct and structured branches
nodes.notes: The direct branch is terminal. The structured branch loses only a $\theta$-dependent constant because $D/d$ is bounded.
nodes.statement_markdown: For arbitrary fixed $\eta>0$, set $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Since $0<d/p<1$ and $$(d/p)^{1-\eta}\ge(d/p)^{1-\theta},$$ the dichotomy and factor aggregation yield constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta(d/p)^{1-\eta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate line-versus-point soundness
nodes.notes: The principal bottlenecks are the bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy and an exact factor-lift proof. Intermediate drafting reductions also require exact audits; work states assert only activity.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, integer $100<d<p$, function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and degree-at-most-$d$ affine-line table, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

summary: Round 2 keeps popularity pruning, the accepted component sampler, and its conditional square-root decoder as a baseline. The accepted integral-cover obstruction and the revise-grade fractional-cover and collision identities rule out specific density-only selector or pair-energy shortcuts, not soundness or every graph-based argument. The near-linear spine asks instead for a label-aware rank-or-decode configuration of mass $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ and integer weight $D=O_\theta(d)$, without requiring a whole-line restriction. The parameter gate makes $D/p=O_\theta(d/p)$ a small fraction of $\epsilon$; rank extraction, reached-root extension, primitive vertical cleanup, and global degree-$D$ peeling then preserve constant mass. Simple roots partition the survivor into at most $D/d=O_\theta(1)$ factor classes while preserving degrees. A standalone seed-point lift would force one heavy factor to be $Z-Q$, after which all disconnected components of that factor aggregate to the same global $Q$ without Vinh mixing. The principal research bottlenecks are the bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy and factor linearization; the intervening drafting reductions also require exact audits and do not constitute verified progress.
target_statement: Convert local line-versus-point agreement into a structured affine-plane incidence configuration with only a $(d/p)^{o(1)}$ loss.
title: Incidence concentration engine
